title: GPU pool live-shrink and maintenance runbook
author: Evan Brooks
body:
Title: GPU pool live-shrink and maintenance runbook

Overview:
This runbook describes the safe procedure for performing live maintenance on Redwood's shared GPU pools with a temporary reduction (live-shrink) in capacity. It covers pre-checks, controlled node/drain steps, traffic rebalancing, alert suppression, verification, rollback, and postmortem guidance. Intended audience: Platform engineers, SREs, and on-call rotation. Estimated typical maintenance window: 30–90 minutes depending on pool size.

Goals:
- Perform planned GPU maintenance or reconfiguration without violating customer latency SLOs.
- Ensure graceful eviction of active inferences with minimal failed requests (<0.1% increase) and no data exposure.
- Enable safe rollback if capacity reduction causes SLA degradation.

Scope:
- Applies to shared clusters backing Redwood Dedicated and hosted inference GPU pools (pools tagged: redwood-gpu-*)
- Not applicable to air-gapped on-prem private deployments (see eng-private-deployments docs)

Assumptions and constraints:
- Target pool is configured with autoscaler and cross-zone redundancy.
- Canary capacity (10–15%) reserved for surge during maintenance.
- A valid maintenance ticket (RFC) exists with scheduled window in PagerDuty calendar.

Roles & ownership:
- Maintenance lead: executes commands and confirms step completions (owner: oncall-platform)
- SRE observer: monitors SLOs, metrics, and alerting (owner: eng-sre)
- Runtime engineer: available for model-serving rollback or model variant routing changes (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Communications: update status page and Slack channel (#platform-maintenance)

Pre-maintenance checklist (complete before T0):
1. Open maintenance RFC and link PagerDuty incident.
2. Confirm canary capacity >= 10% of pool during window.
3. Identify nodes to remove (node IDs) and validate health.
4. Notify customers via scheduled maintenance notices if required by SLA.
5. Create a rollback plan and snapshot any autoscaler configs.
6. Save golden prompts and synthetic traffic runners for verification.

Monitoring & dashboards to watch:
- dashboards: GPU pool capacity (redwood/gpu/pool/{pool}/capacity)
- request latency p50/p95/p99 per-route
- error rate per model and per-token
- queue depth and inference backlog
- autoscaler decision logs
- live KV cache hit ratio

Thresholds that trigger immediate rollback:
- p99 latency increase > 30% relative to baseline for 5 minutes
- error rate > 0.3% absolute increase over baseline for 5 minutes
- queue backlog growth > 50% and not draining in 10 minutes
- model-serving nodes dropping below configured failover minimum

High-level procedure (T0 is maintenance start):
1) T-30m: Final validation and alert suppression
- Mute non-actionable alerts via Alertmanager silence (note silence ID).
- Post a status note in #platform-maintenance and open incident in PagerDuty.

2) T0: Reserve surge/canary capacity
- Verify canary reservations are active:
  - CLI: rwdctl pool reserve --pool <pool> --percent 15 --reason "maintenance"
  - Confirm reservation displayed on dashboard.

3) T+5m: Begin phased drain of selected nodes
- For each node (do nodes one-at-a-time unless extra capacity exists):
  a) Mark node as schedulable=false in orchestration layer:
     - kubectl cordon <node-name>
  b) Initiate graceful eviction of running inference containers:
     - rwdctl node drain --node <node-name> --grace-period 600
  c) Watch backlog and in-flight requests until drain success or timeout.
  d) If drain exceeds 20 minutes and backlog not dropping, abort and rollback.

4) T+X: Reconfigure autoscaler and capacity policies if required
- Apply temporary scaling policy to prefer horizontal buffer:
  - Terraform example (apply with -target to avoid full replans):

```hcl
resource "rwd_autoscaler_policy" "pool-temp-buffer" {
  pool_id = "<pool>"
  min_nodes = var.min_nodes
  buffer_percent = 25
  note = "Temporary buffer for maintenance"
}
```

- Command: terraform apply -target=rwd_autoscaler_policy.pool-temp-buffer

5) Confirm model-serving health and route balancing
- Validate per-model throughput is within 10% of baseline.
- If specific model variants are overloaded, perform temporary routing to warm variants:
  - rwdctl route set --model <model> --variant <warm-variant> --weight 0.4

6) Complete maintenance action (kernel update/reimage/taint)
- Perform the required action on drained node (example: reimage via image-builder).
- After action, uncordon and return node to pool:
  - kubectl uncordon <node-name>

Post-maintenance verification:
- Run synthetic traffic runner for 5 minutes and compare latencies to baseline.
- Verify autoscaler logs show expected scaling decisions.
- Confirm no high-severity alerts in last 15 minutes.
- Remove temporary autoscaler policy and confirm config drift is reconciled.

Rollback procedure (if thresholds hit):
1. Immediately stop further drains.
2. Reopen paused nodes by cancelling maintenance operations.
3. Revert any temporary routing or Terraform changes using saved plan snapshots.
4. Re-enable paused alerts and escalate to incident commander.
5. If capacity loss persists, trigger cross-region failover per the cross-region-fallback runbook.

Communications and customer impact notes:
- Post timeline and impact details to status.redwood.ai and #platform-maintenance.
- For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, follow dedicated-customer-communication playbook in customer-success-and-support.

Postmortem and retro actions (within 72 hours):
- Collect logs, metric snapshots, and autoscaler decisions.
- Run retrospective with stakeholders and update this runbook for lessons learned.
- Required retro fields: root cause, mitigation, preventive action, owner, ETA.

Appendices:
- Useful commands:
  - kubectl cordon/uncordon/drain
  - rwdctl pool reserve/pool release/node drain/route set
  - terraform plan/apply with -target
- Known limitations:
  - Live-shrink increases complexity for cold-start heavy models.
  - Some private deployments require separate maintenance procedures.

Related pages:
- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/scheduled-maintenance-coordination-and-rollback-runbook-2024
- /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/gpu-pool-sizing-guidelines-2025

Owners & contact:
- oncall-platform@redwood.ai (primary)
- eng-sre@redwood.ai (observer)
- #platform-maintenance (Slack channel)

Document revision history:
- 2025-11-04: Created by Evan Brooks
- 2026-02-15: Updated thresholds and added Terraform snippet (Evan Brooks)

End of runbook.
